title: Taking a Step When Pushed: The Capture Point, Where a Foot Must Land, and How the Time to Get It There Limits the Push That Can Be Answered

questions.question: What is the capture point?
options: The place where the body's centre of mass is now
The furthest place the swinging foot can reach
The place on the ground over which the body would come to rest, x plus v times the time constant
The place where the centre of pressure is
questions.explanation: It is the pendulum's own stopping place: put the support there and the body comes to rest over it. Nearer, and the body carries on over the foot.

questions.question: A push of 0.30 m/s put the capture point how far out?
options: 5.0 cm
30 cm, the speed times one second
16.6 cm, the time constant
questions.explanation: 0.30 m/s times a time constant of 0.166 s. That is where a foot would need to be if it could land at once.

questions.question: Why must the foot land further than the capture point of the push?
options: Because the foot slides after it lands
Because the leg is longest when stretched out to the side
To leave room for the next step
The capture point runs away exponentially while the foot is in the air
questions.explanation: The swing takes time, and in 0.25 s the capture point had gone from 5.0 cm to more than 22 cm. The foot has to be aimed at where it will be, plus a margin.

questions.question: The largest push that could be answered with a swing of 0.35 s:
options: 0.30 m/s, the push of the test
questions.explanation: Reach is fixed at 25 cm, and the longer the swing the further the capture point has run. 0.56 m/s at 0.15 s, 0.31 at 0.25 s, 0.17 at 0.35 s.

questions.question: Why is a fast swing worth so much?
options: The capture point grows exponentially with the swing time
A fast swing puts the foot down harder, which brakes the body
A fast swing uses less of the servos' heat
The leg reaches further in a fast swing
questions.explanation: The target moves away exponentially, 2.7 times for each time constant, so time saved in the air is worth more than length added to the leg.

questions.question: When is a step the right answer?
options: For every push, since a step always works
Only when the body is already standing still
When the push is beyond what the feet's moments can answer (35-05)
When the push is small enough for the leg to reach its target
questions.explanation: The feet's forces answer small pushes without moving a foot. A step is for what they cannot supply, and it has its own limit in reach and swing time.
